summary: American record producer Phil Spector, creator of the Wall of Sound, cheated collaborators, kept his wife Ronnie Spector a virtual prisoner, menaced many people with guns and in 2003 shot actress Lana Clarkson dead at his California home.

evidence.note: born December 1939 in the Bronx to Jewish immigrant families
writes and produces his first number-one hit with the Teddy Bears in 1958
Brill Building collaborators say he grabbed credit and cut them out of royalties
releases records under a girl group's name without the group singing on them
wedding-night rage leaves Ronnie and her mother hiding in a bathroom
shows Ronnie a gold casket as a threat of what awaits her if she leaves; house kept locked
flown to London in 1969 to rework the Beatles' Let It Be tapes, then Harrison and Lennon albums
1975 guilty plea for pulling a gun on a parking attendant; probation ignored
night of 2 February 2003: meets Lana Clarkson at the House of Blues
detailed description of Clarkson's gunshot wound and the crime scene
2009 retrial ends in a second-degree murder conviction, 19 years to life
dies in prison; Ronnie outlives him by about two years

notes: Guest Greazy Will narrates; Robert listens. Death year 2021 from general knowledge (transcript only places it about two years before Ronnie's death). labor-exploitation is a loose fit for royalty theft and replacing singers. Abuse of his adopted sons (locked rooms, forced sexual simulations) is covered only briefly, so no child-abuse theme. GB is a secondary setting for the Beatles work; scope kept national.
